original_test_intent: Prove the first populated HPM (HPM0/1P configuration) is physically connected to the intended BMC I2C-2 management path and that the BMC can safely address and read every required HPM0 device through the correct controller, mux and downstream channel.
original_method: Bind the logical I2C-2 label to the exact BMC controller, OS/vendor adapter, mux chain/channel, HPM0 connector and 1P population state; obtain the expected 7-bit address, stable identity register/value and safe read transaction for each device; have an operator verify and photograph the powered-down or vendor-approved live physical connection; preserve baseline bus/BMC logs; execute only allowlisted non-destructive discovery and identity reads; compare the complete observed map and responses with the HPM0 oracle and stop on first bus error without blind reset or retry.
manual_activity: An operator confirms HPM0 is the first populated HPM/1P target, verifies the connector/cable seating under the vendor service procedure and supplies photos; software evidence cannot replace this physical checkpoint.
required_inputs: Authoritative logical I2C-2 to BMC controller/adapter/mux/channel/HPM0 connector map
First-HPM 1P population and expected device table with 7-bit addresses, safe identity registers/masks and values
Vendor-approved non-destructive discovery/read procedure and prohibited-address/command list
Physical inspection state, service safety, BMC access, bus-error acceptance and recovery
safety_requirements: Operate only through the approved BMC/OOB path; do not assume a host adapter or literal adapter number
Do not use quick-write probing or read unknown registers; never write EEPROM or control registers
Preserve BMC and bus logs and keep the management path stable during inspection
Stop on timeout, NACK pattern outside oracle, stuck bus, arbitration/error storm, unexpected device, BMC instability or topology ambiguity
No automatic rescan/reset/retry after a bus fault
agent_execution_scope: Validate controller/mux/channel and expected HPM0 identity map plus allowlisted transactions
Collect read-only target-bound bus/address/identity and BMC error evidence after operator physical confirmation
Report missing, unexpected or mismatched devices without manipulating the bus or connector
Do not guess I2C-2 adapter syntax, probe unknown devices, perform writes, reset the BMC/bus or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the exact I2C-2 controller/mux/channel/HPM0 connector and 1P device oracle
Approve safe commands/registers, error tolerance, physical service procedure and recovery
Review software and physical evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: i2cdetect/i2cget are plausible only after mapping the logical bus and approving safe transactions; `i2cdetect -y I2C-2` is not a valid universally safe or necessarily syntactically correct target.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the owner-approved BMC/vendor read-only method on the mapped controller/mux/channel and query only allowlisted HPM0 addresses/registers, retaining the complete map, identity responses and bus-health evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC I2C-2 to HPM0 first-HPM/1P functional scope, AI_VR_I2C_bus2 bundle, and 10/10-minute allocation remain; no adapter number, address or register is invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: MEDIUM HYBRID PHYSICAL AND BMC I2C HPM0 FUNCTIONAL CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Combine an operator-confirmed physical path with a controller/mux-bound allowlist of read-only device identity transactions and correlated BMC bus-error state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact management topology, device/register oracle, transaction safety, independent physical evidence and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An address ACK alone can come from the wrong mux channel or device and does not prove HPM0 identity or 1P functional connectivity; photos alone cannot prove communication.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some I2C devices react to SMBus quick commands or register reads, so generic scanning can alter or hang a live BMC management bus.

project_override_considerations: A vendor BMC inventory command may replace raw i2c-tools only if it proves the same controller/channel and stable device identities. Host-side I2C enumeration or a generic address map does not establish the required BMC HPM0 path.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, owner approval and HPM0 first-HPM/1P population record
Operator physical-connection photos tied to connector/path identity and timestamp
BMC controller/adapter/mux/channel map and expected address/register/value allowlist
Exact approved commands and complete observed address plus identity-response table
Pre/post BMC/I2C timeout/NACK/arbitration/stuck-bus logs and unchanged management health
Discrepancy/recovery record and engineer PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED decision

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, Criteria and bundle consistently target BMC I2C-2 communication with HPM0 in the first-HPM/1P state. The related path label is context that must be mapped, not a competing objective.

review_improvement: Prevents a logical bus label or unsafe generic scan from substituting for the exact BMC-to-HPM0 physical path and safe device-identity proof.
independent_technical_reasoning: I2C bus labels are platform abstractions and may traverse BMC adapters and muxes, so a literal scan target cannot be inferred from 'I2C-2'. An ACK is also insufficient because multiple devices can share addresses on different channels. The functional result therefore needs both independently verified physical connectivity and identity-bearing reads on the exact mapped path. Transaction allowlisting is essential because generic detection methods can issue commands that live VRs, EEPROMs or controllers do not tolerate.
